sentences: The doctor, whose wife is now visibly pregnant, finds an unkempt detective in a crack house under the influence of drugs.
The doctor attempts to force him to rehabilitate, but the detective insists that he was undercover for a case.
The detective's brother confronts the detective about the drug use and realises that the detective is investigating the blackmailer, a newspaper owner who blackmails people.
A noblewoman has enlisted the detective to negotiate the return of stolen letters written by the noblewoman's husband.
The detective's brother warns the detective not to go after the blackmailer, which the detective ignores.
The doctor is also surprised to discover that the detective is in a relationship with the doctor's wife's bridesmaid.
The detective tells the doctor that he is dating her because she is the blackmailer's assistant.
He uses their relationship to enable him to break into the blackmailer's office in the city.
Inside, the detective and the doctor find an incapacitated bridesmaid, and the detective happens upon the doctor's wife holding the blackmailer at gunpoint.
The doctor's wife shoots the detective, who harnesses all his mental powers to stay conscious.
He is taken to a hospital, where he flatlines on the operating table.
But in his mind palace, the criminal mastermind taunts the detective that he's letting the doctor down by dying, which convinces him to revive.
When the detective wakes up in surgery, he mouths the name of the doctor's wife.
The doctor meets his wife at the hospital and tells her that the detective survived.
The doctor's wife visits the dazed and severely injured detective and warns him not to denounce her.

The doctor nonetheless begins to suspect something after discovering that the detective moved the doctor's chair in the detective's flat back to its usual spot and left a bottle of the doctor's wife's perfume on the table next to it.
The detective breaks out from the hospital and arranges a meeting with the doctor's wife.
He tells her he knows she has stolen the identity of a baby who died in 1972.
He deduces that she intentionally shot him in a non-lethal spot and, using a ruse, exposes the doctor's wife's secret life as an assassin to the doctor.
Back at the detective's flat the doctor angrily confronts his wife, asking what he ever did to deserve her.
The detective tells the doctor that he's observed his addiction to danger, and his attraction to the doctor's wife complies with this fact.
She tells them some of her past and that the blackmailer has information that would send her to prison for the rest of her life.
The doctor's wife gives the doctor a memory stick marked with the initials.
The stick, which she says contains everything about her and would destroy his love for her.
The detective tells the doctor he can trust his wife because she saved his life by calling an ambulance after shooting him.
After ignoring the memory stick for several months, the doctor burns it without reading it and reconciles with his wife.

The couple is spending Christmas with the two brothers at their parents' home, where the detective takes the opportunity to drug everyone but the doctor so that they can steal the detective's brother's laptop.
The detective takes a hesitant doctor to meet the blackmailer at his estate, which he believes contains the blackmailer's blackmail archive.

During their confrontation, the blackmailer reveals that he was behind the kidnapping of the doctor, as seen in an earlier episode and explains that he put pressure on the doctor's wife in order to "own" the detective's brother via the doctor and the detective.
The detective offers to trade the blackmailer's information on the doctor's wife for the state secrets contained in the detective's brother's laptop.
However, the blackmailer is aware that the detective is setting him up in a trap.

The laptop contains a GPS tracker, and once the detective's brother realises it is gone, security services will raid the estate and, upon finding the laptop, will have a legal reason to search the blackmail archives.
With visible joy, the blackmailer reveals that the plan will not work because his vaults don't physically exist; the data are in his mind palace.
As a newspaper publisher, he can publicise any secret without backup documents.
By giving the blackmailer the laptop, the detective and the doctor are now guilty of selling government secrets.
They can be imprisoned for high treason, whereas the blackmailer remains legally untouchable.
When the detective's brother and the police arrive, the detective coldly shoots the blackmailer in the head, realising that this is the only way to free his friends and everyone else from his power.
The detective's brother convinces the government to spare the detective a trial and, as an alternative punishment, press him into a high-risk mission in a distant region.

However, within minutes of taking off, the detective is recalled when video screens all over the country begin to broadcast a loop of a static image of the criminal mastermind asking "Did you miss me?".
In the post-credits scene, the criminal mastermind breaks the fourth wall and asks the audience if they missed him as well.
The detective and the doctor receive a visit from a client, who witnessed his father's being killed by a "gigantic hound" on the moor 20 years ago.
After years of therapy, the client revisited the site, only to see the hound's footprints, prompting his request for help.
Though initially dismissive, the detective is soon intrigued by the client's use of "hound" instead of "dog".
The detective and the doctor arrive on the moor to find that the hound is a local legend.
They visit the facility, a nearby defence ministry research base, using the detective's brother's security pass.
After the detective's brother's credentials cause a security alert, a scientist vouches for the detective's identity, despite knowing the truth.
The scientist says he was a friend of the client's father and is concerned for the client's well-being.
The client tells the doctor and the detective about the words "liberty" and "in" in his dreams.
The detective, the doctor, and the client then visit the hollow in the hope of finding the hound.
On the way, the doctor hangs back to observe what seems to be coded signals but these prove to be unrelated to the case.
When he catches up to the detective and the client, the client says that he has just seen the hound in the thick fog and that the detective must have seen it, too, which the detective denies.
Later, at a local inn, the detective is visibly shaken and confesses he did see the hound.
The doctor tries calming him, suggesting he imagined it, but the detective reacts with anger, denying there is anything wrong with him.
The doctor leaves him alone and tries to pump the client's therapist for information, under the guise of chatting her up.
However, they are interrupted by the scientist, who blows his cover.
Meanwhile, the client hallucinates that the hound is stalking his home.
The next morning the detective theorizes that "hound" may be an acronym rather than a word.
The pair run into a police inspector who was sent by the detective's brother to keep an eye on the detective.
They interrogate the innkeepers about a past order for meat that the doctor spotted, which struck him as odd for a vegetarian restaurant.
The innkeepers admit keeping a dog on the moor to boost the tourist trade, but pretend to the investigators that it had been put down.
This explanation satisfies the police inspector but not the detective, who insists that the dog he saw was monstrous.
Calling the detective's brother, the detective gains access to the facility again.
Searching the lower levels of the genetics labs alone, the doctor finds himself trapped and then hears growling, which he assumes is the hound.
Locking himself in an empty cage, he calls the detective, who rescues him.
The detective deduces that a chemical weapon designed to trigger violent hallucinations was responsible.
Retreating into his "mind palace", a memory technique, the detective realises that "liberty" and "in" stand for a town and its state.
After viewing confidential files, he learns that the acronym was a secret intelligence agency project aimed at creating a hallucinatory anti-personnel chemical weapon.
Although the project was abandoned several years before, the detective realises the scientist, who participated in the project, has continued it secretly.

After the doctor receives a call from the therapist warning that the client has run off with a gun, the doctor, the detective, and the police inspector run to the hollow to find the client about to commit suicide.
The detective explains that the hound was a hallucination; his father had been killed by the scientist, wearing a gas mask and a sweatshirt with "the acronym.
The town and its state" on it.
A child could not cope with this, so his mind tricked him.
Every time the client came back, the scientist gassed him with the hallucinogen.
The fog in the hollow is actually the chemical agent, triggered by pressure pads in the area.
As the client calms down, they all fall under the influence of the gas and see a savage dog preparing to attack them, and the doctor shoots it.
The scientist appears at the scene, and the detective briefly hallucinates that he is the criminal mastermind, before giving chase.
The client realises that his father had been murdered because he found the scientist testing the drug.
He attacks the scientist, who flees into the base's minefield and is blown up.
As the detective and the doctor prepare to leave the following day, the doctor wonders why he saw the hound in the laboratory despite not having inhaled the gas from the hollow.
The detective surmises that the leaking pipes poisoned the doctor in the laboratory.
The detective remains distant to the doctor, who is still grieving over the death of his wife.
The doctor, who is seeing a new therapist, conceals the fact that he is having hallucinations of his wife.
The tycoon, a prominent entrepreneur and philanthropist, gathers close colleagues, including his daughter, to confess that he is going to kill somebody.
Before he does so, he forcibly injects them with a serum that inhibits memory.
The tycoon's daughter is still able to remember fragments and writes them down on a sheet of paper.
She comes to the detective, who has started abusing drugs again, and says that she remembers one word that shook her.
The detective dismisses her case as being too weird and refers her to the police.
Before the tycoon's daughter leaves, the detective realises that she is suicidal and offers to walk with her around the city.
The detective's brother tracks the detective's movement across the city and calls the doctor out of concern, accidentally implying existence of another sibling in the family.
The detective and the tycoon's daughter walk all night, and the following morning he decides to take her case.
The detective is momentarily overwhelmed by the side effects of his drug use and, upon gathering himself, finds the tycoon's daughter gone.
As the detective stumbles back to his flat, he realises that the "one word" was "anyone".
The tycoon is a serial killer with the wealth and power to hide his crimes completely.
The detective becomes obsessed with the tycoon and publicly accuses him of being a serial killer, but his drug-addled antics frighten the landlady.
She subdues him and brings him to see the doctor while he is at his therapist's house for a session.

Much to the doctor's shock and annoyance, the arrival at his therapist's house of a car sent by the tycoon and then of a pathologist with an ambulance were all prearranged by the detective two weeks prior, even before the doctor had chosen his new therapist.

The detective and the doctor are brought to a studio where they meet with the tycoon, who reveals he has used the detective's accusation as a publicity stunt to support his new brand of cereal, saying he's a "Cereal Killer".
He claims the detective was in on the joke and then takes them to visit a new hospital wing for which he had been a major donor.
The tycoon then takes the detective and the doctor to his 'favourite room', whilst repeatedly mentioning a 19th century serial killer.
The doctor asks the tycoon how he moves through all of the rooms freely, to which the tycoon replies that he has keys to the hospital.
As the detective tries to goad the tycoon into a confession, the tycoon's daughter arrives, having been texted by the detective from the tycoon's phone.
Upon seeing her, the detective realises that she was not the woman who had come to his flat.
Frustrated and suffering from withdrawal, the detective attacks the tycoon with a scalpel, but is stopped by the doctor, who attacks the detective in anger, blaming him for the doctor's wife's death.
The detective is admitted into the tycoon's hospital, where the doctor pays him a last visit.
After the doctor leaves, the tycoon enters the detective's room through a secret door.
The detective asks the tycoon to kill him and directs him to change the dosage on his intravenous machine.
The detective induces the tycoon to confess to his murders, and the tycoon begins to suffocate him.
But the doctor burst into the room, having been alerted by his wife's video, asking him to "save the doctor" by "going to Hell".
Unknown to the tycoon, the events were part of the detective's elaborate plot to expose the tycoon and fulfill the doctor's wife's last request.
The doctor pulls the tycoon off the detective.

The tycoon claims he was trying to help the detective, but the detective reveals a recording device hidden in the doctor's walking stick, which he had left behind earlier, that recorded the tycoon's boasting confession.
While the recording might not be admissible evidence, the tycoon soon finds he enjoys confessing to the police inspector.
The doctor reconciles with the detective, telling him that he no longer blames him for his wife's death.
He also confesses to the detective – and to his hallucination of his wife – that he had cheated on her by texting with another woman.
The detective comforts him as he weeps, and his wife finally disappears.
After resuming taking cases, the detective discovers the note "the tycoon's daughter" had left behind, proving the woman was real and not a drug-induced hallucination.
Upon inspecting the note under a black light the detective finds the message "Miss me?".
During the doctor's next session, his therapist reveals she was both the woman with whom he had been texting and the one who pretended to be the tycoon's daughter.
Holding the doctor at gunpoint, she reveals herself to be the detective and the detective's brother's secret sibling.
As the doctor attempts to leave, the secret sibling pulls the trigger.
The doctor is in his first meeting with his therapist after eighteen months.
Struggling to explain the reason for his visit, he eventually chokes out the words, "My best friend, the detective, is dead".

The episode flashes back to three months earlier, with the detective receiving plaudits and gifts from various people for whom he has solved cases, along with much-unwanted media attention, especially for his recovery of a famous artist's painting of a waterfall.
Meanwhile, the villain uses his mobile phone to simultaneously break into the case where the royal jewels are kept, open the vault at the national bank and unlock all the cells at a large prison.
Before smashing the royal jewels' case, he writes the words "Get the detective" on the outside, to be seen by the security cameras.
He then allows himself to be caught by the police wearing the jewels and sitting on the throne.
The detective is called to testify at the villain's trial, where he explains that the villain is a criminal mastermind.
The villain has threatened the jurors with the deaths of their families, leading them to vote "not guilty".
After being acquitted, the villain visits the detective and explains that his break-in was a publicity stunt to show potential clients what he is capable of, adding, "I owe you a fall."

Meanwhile, the doctor is summoned to see the detective's brother, who explains that four professional assassins have moved into flats on the detective's street and asks him to watch out for the detective.
The detective and the doctor investigate the kidnapping of the children of the British Ambassador to another country.

The detective deciphers evidence allowing the police to find the children, but as part of a plot to make others suspect that the detective has been staging his cases himself, the villain has traumatised the girl, so she is terrified of the detective when she sees him.
A police sergeant begins to suspect the detective.
The chief superintendent forces a reluctant police inspector to arrest the detective, but he escapes with the doctor handcuffed as his 'hostage'.
They realise the villain's "Get the detective" has convinced the criminal underworld that the villain has given the detective the computer code he used to pull off his triple heist.
This code is supposedly capable of bypassing all security systems.
The detective and the doctor break into the house of a journalist, who is poised to publish an exposé on the detective.
They find that the villain has created a fake identity, an invented persona (the waterfall's name in German), an actor whom the detective supposedly paid to pose as a master criminal.
Now a wanted man with his media image on the verge of plummeting, the detective launches a final gambit.
Leaving the doctor, the detective contacts a colleague, a pathologist at the hospital, and admits that, contrary to her belief, he respects her and has always trusted her.
He tells the pathologist he is in grave danger and humbly asks her for help.

The doctor goes to a gentlemen's club to question the detective's brother and learns that the detective's brother unintentionally divulged the detective's personal information during his interrogations of the villain.
Meanwhile, the detective deduces that the anti-security code was encoded in the tapping of the villain's fingers during his earlier visit.
The doctor finds the detective at the hospital lab but leaves after hearing the landlady has been shot.
The detective texts the villain, inviting him to meet him on the hospital roof to solve their "final problem".
The detective claims that he can electronically erase the invented persona with the code.
But the villain reveals that there is no code; he simply bribed security guards.
He gives the detective an ultimatum: the detective must commit suicide or the villain's hitmen will kill the doctor, the landlady, and the police inspector.
The detective realizes the villain has a way to prevent the executions and convinces the villain that he is willing to do anything to make him stop the assassins.
After acknowledging their similarities, the villain tells the detective, "As long as I am alive, you can save your friends".
He then commits suicide by shooting himself, effectively closing the detective's options for saving his friends other than jumping from the roof.
Afterward, the detective calls the doctor, who is rushing back from their flat after finding the landlady was safe.

Claiming that he was always a fake and explaining this last phone call is his "note", the detective swan-dives off the roof of the hospital, as the doctor looks on terrified from the street, thereby ensuring that the villain's true identity dies with him.
After being knocked to the ground by a cyclist, the doctor stumbles over to watch, grief-stricken, as the detective's bloody corpse is carried away by hospital staff.
The episode returns to the doctor's therapy session, where he cannot open up.
The detective's brother is shown reading a tabloid newspaper with a front-page headline "Suicide of Fake Genius".
Later, the doctor visits the detective's grave with the landlady.
He reaffirms his faith in the detective and begs him not to be dead.
As he walks away, the detective looks on from afar, out of the doctor's sight, before also walking away.
During a dangerous confrontation, the detective, the doctor and the criminal mastermind are interrupted by a call on the criminal mastermind's phone.
He withdraws and dismisses his snipers.
The detective becomes a celebrity after the doctor blogs about their cases.
One day, they are brought to meet the detective's brother in the royal palace.
The detective's brother reveals that a dominatrix took compromising photographs of a female member of the royal family.
The authority wants to retrieve the dominatrix's smartphone, which contains those photographs.
The detective and the doctor try to get into the dominatrix's home by deception, but she expects them.
The dominatrix meets the detective nude, leaving him unable to deduce anything about her.
She tells him she does not intend to blackmail her client, but the photographs are her "protection".
The doctor triggers the fire alarm, enabling the detective to find the dominatrix's hidden safe.
Suddenly several intelligence agency operatives led by a senior agent break into the house and demand that the detective open the safe.
The detective solves the password, which triggers a trap that kills one agent and allows them to break free.
The detective gets the phone first, but the dominatrix injects him with a sedative, takes the phone, and escapes.
On Christmas Eve, the detective receives a package containing the dominatrix's phone, which is password locked.
Considering its importance to her, the detective thinks she is about to be killed.
The police find a body with a mutilated face, which the detective identifies as the dominatrix.
On New Year's Eve, the doctor is brought to the dominatrix, who faked her death.
She tells him she needs the phone back but refuses to let the detective know she is alive.
However, the detective followed the doctor and sees her.
When he arrives back at the detective's flat, the detective finds the senior agent's team holding the landlady hostage, but he subdues the senior agent and pushes him out of the window.
Months later, the dominatrix appears at the detective's flat and reveals that she is still being hunted.
She asks the detective to decipher a code stolen from a member of the defence ministry.
The detective reveals it to be airline seat numbers and deduces it applies to a flight leaving the airport the next day.
The dominatrix secretly conveys this information to the criminal mastermind, who taunts the detective's brother that he now knows their plan.
A government official brings the detective to the airport.
The detective's brother confirms that the government planned to fly a plane full of corpses to avoid alerting terrorists that they knew the plane would be bombed, reminiscent of a wartime myth.
However, as the detective unwittingly helped the dominatrix (and thus the criminal mastermind) crack the code, the scheme failed.
The dominatrix appears and gives the detective's brother a list of demands, including protection, in exchange for the contents of her phone.
However, the detective deduces the phone password is part of his own name, so the screen reads as a pun on it.
Without her leverage, the dominatrix pleads for protection, but the detective and the detective's brother turn her down.

Some months later, the detective's brother gives the doctor the dominatrix's phone and tells him that – although he intends to tell the detective that she has entered a witness protection programme in another country – the dominatrix actually has been killed by terrorists.
Up in their flat, the detective asks the doctor for the dominatrix's phone and says that her last text message to him was "Goodbye, detective," suggesting her death.
After the doctor leaves, a flashback shows that the detective was disguised as the executioner and rescued the dominatrix.
A police inspector and a police sergeant are on the verge of arresting a criminal family that has evaded the police several times.

However, when the police inspector receives a text from the detective asking for help, he tells the police sergeant to make the arrest herself and races to the detective's flat, assuming the worst and calling for full backup – only to discover that the detective is simply struggling to write a best man speech for the doctor's upcoming wedding to the bride.
On the morning of the wedding, the landlady reminds the detective that marriage changes people.
The detective calls his brother, who repeats the landlady's suggestion that the doctor and the bride's marriage will change his life.
At the reception, the doctor is delighted to see a major, his former Army CO.
The major (the name is a reference to a character in an earlier novel) lives in seclusion, having received death threats and media scrutiny after losing a unit of new soldiers in a distant country.

The detective rises to give the best man speech, and begins by reading from the wedding telegrams, after which he expresses his deep love and respect for the doctor and launches into a rambling narrative, describing the doctor's role in an attempted murder case, "the Bloody Guardsman".
A Guardsman had contacted the detective, fearing he was being stalked.
When the detective and the doctor arrived at the Guards' quarters, the Guardsman was found seemingly stabbed to death in a locked shower stall with no weapon in the room.
The doctor insisted on being allowed to examine the Guardsman's body, discovered he was still breathing, and requested an ambulance.
The detective says the most remarkable thing about the case was that, while he had focused on trying to solve a murder (he admits that it remains unsolved), the doctor had saved a life.
The detective's narrative drifts to the case of "the Mayfly Man".
Several days after going to a man's apartment for a romantic dinner, a woman, who works as a private nurse, found the apartment was vacated and the man had died weeks ago.
The detective and the doctor, still inebriated from the doctor's stag night, attempt to search the flat for clues but are arrested for their drunken antics.
The next morning, an amused police inspector secures their release.
Following up something the nurse said, the detective contacts other women in the city with a similar experience and realizes that all of them have service jobs – such as gardener, cook, or maid.

The doctor's knowledge of human nature lets the detective conclude that the perpetrator is a man bored with marriage, who adopts the names of recently deceased single men and uses their unoccupied homes to meet women.
While finally beginning his toast to the couple, the detective suddenly freezes, recalling that the nurse had known the doctor's middle name.
Aware that the doctor hates and never uses it, he deduces that the nurse could only have seen it on the wedding invitation.
The detective concludes that all the women had worked for the major in various capacities and were bound by confidentiality agreements.
The Mayfly Man had courted them to find and attack the major and plans to strike at the wedding.
The detective slips a note to the major, who locks himself in his hotel room and arms himself.
The detective, the doctor, and the bride race after him but he refuses to open the door until the detective finds the solution.
He deduces that the Bloody Guardsman case is linked to the major's and pinpoints the military uniform both wore as the common link.

The detective deduces that the Guardsman had been stabbed while on duty, with a stiletto-type blade through his belt, which being worn tightly around the waist, prevented him from feeling his injury and also held the flesh together, so damage did not take effect until he removed it.
Upon hearing this explanation, the major considers suicide by releasing his belt and bleeding to death.
The detective persuades him not to, primarily because it would be cruel to do at the doctor's wedding.
The major then opens the door and requests medical assistance.
The detective has the police inspector apprehend the wedding photographer and identifies him as the Mayfly Man, deducing he was the only person who could have stabbed the major.
The photographer's brother had been one of the men killed under the major's command, and he stabbed the Guardsman as practice for this murder.
After the arrest the wedding reception resumes, and the detective plays the violin for the doctor and the bride's first dance.
Afterward he quietly reveals to them that he has observed the bride's "increased appetite, change in taste perception, and sickness in the morning, the signs of three", revealing she is pregnant.
The detective calms them by explaining that they will make great parents since they've had plenty of practice with him.
Despite the happy revelation, the episode ends on a bittersweet note.
The detective leaves the reception alone upon realizing that his relationship with the doctor will never be the same again.

The detective's brother presents doctored footage of the newspaper magnate (in an earlier episode) being shot, so that it will appear to the public as though the newspaper magnate was shot accidentally by a sniper.
The detective and a committee chaired by a noblewoman are attending.
The detective is freed, and resolves to wait for the criminal mastermind's posthumous revenge.
The doctor's wife gives birth to a daughter, who is named after her mother.
The doctor befriends a woman he met on a bus.
He starts an intense texting relationship with her but eventually puts a stop to it.
The detective's brother and police detectives including a police inspector bring the detective various cases, hoping they will reveal the criminal mastermind's scheme.
One case involves the son of a cabinet minister.
The son is found dead in a car crash outside their home, despite having been on a gap year in a distant country.
The detective quickly solves the case, and reveals that the son was hiding in the car, planning to surprise his father, but died from a seizure.
A week later, a drunk driver crashed into the car.
The detective notes that a bust of a former prime minister at the minister's home was missing from its place and finds that it had been stolen and smashed upon the front porch.
In the following weeks, five other busts made in the series were also smashed.
In one instance, someone was killed.
Staking out the location of the last one, the detective encounters a culprit.
They fight, but the culprit escapes.
In the centre of the last bust is a memory stick labelled with initials, like the one the doctor's wife had given to the doctor.
Questioned by the detective, the doctor's wife relates her past as a freelance agent on a team called by those initials.
Each had a memory stick containing their confidential material, lest anyone be betrayed by another.

Six years prior, a rescue mission of hostages held at the British embassy in a foreign capital went wrong when the captors were tipped off and killed everyone on the team except her former teammate and the doctor's wife.
The detective tries to stop the doctor's wife from going after her former teammate, but the doctor's wife drugs him and escapes.
The doctor's wife travels across the world following a random path that "not even the detective could follow."
But having planted a tracking device in the memory stick, the detective and the doctor intercept her in a faraway country.
Her former teammate arrives, having followed the detective, and attempts to kill all three.

He reveals that, while being tortured and held in the foreign capital, his captors kept taunting him with the word "Ammo" and told him he'd been betrayed by "the English woman", whom he assumed to be the doctor's wife.
He escaped, having hidden his memory stick in a half-made bust, then sought revenge on the doctor's wife, believing that she had betrayed them.
The standoff is broken up by local police, who shoot her former teammate.
The detective deduces that 'Ammo' should be Amo, the Latin word for "I love", which suggests the noblewoman, whose code name is Love.
Questioned by the detective's brother, the noblewoman claims to be innocent.
The detective meets the noblewoman's assistant in the city aquarium.
The assistant confesses that she tipped the terrorists off in that country, using the code "Amo", thus eliminating the hostages and the agent team.
Her motive was killing the British ambassador, who found that she had sold national secrets.
The doctor, the detective's brother and the police arrive, and the assistant shoots at the detective, but the doctor's wife jumps in the way, taking the bullet.
The doctor's wife professes her love and gratitude to the doctor and the detective and dies.
The doctor, grief-stricken, blames the detective, who had vowed to protect the doctor's wife.
In his home, the detective's brother finds a sticky note reading "13th" and places a call to a secret contact.
The detective visits the doctor's therapist but is unable to open up to her.
The landlady gives the detective a DVD, which contains a posthumous message from the doctor's wife.
In the video, the doctor's wife asks the detective to 'Save the doctor'.
The detective attempts to visit the doctor, but a friend gives him a note from the doctor and tells him that the doctor would rather have anyone's help but the detective's.
The doctor, an army doctor injured in a distant country, meets the detective, who is looking for someone to share a flat on a city street, owned by a landlady.
The police, led by a detective inspector, have been baffled by a series of deaths, described as "serial suicides".
The detective is invited to inspect the latest crime scene, that of a woman dressed exclusively in pink, who managed to claw a few letters into the floor before dying.

The detective deduces that the word was a girl's name and that the woman was from out of town; observing that her luggage is not at the crime scene, he searches the neighborhood until he finds it, discarded by the killer.
The luggage tag reveals her name and gives her phone number.
With this information the detective learns that the girl's name was the name of the victim's deceased daughter.
Meanwhile, the doctor is compelled to meet a man who claims to be the detective's "arch-enemy".
The man offers him money to spy on the detective, but the doctor refuses.
The man also tells the doctor that, contrary to what his therapist believes, the doctor is not suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder but in fact misses being in combat.
When the doctor returns to the flat, the detective asks him to text the victim's still-missing phone, hoping the murderer will make a move.

The detective presumes that the victim planted her phone on the killer so that he could be traced by GPS; correctly assuming that the girl's name was her password, he initiates such a search through her online account and finds the signal at the flat.
The detective finds a taxi waiting for him on the street, and the cabbie confesses to the murders but proclaims he merely speaks to his victims, and they kill themselves.
The cabbie challenges the detective to play his game, and drives him to a secluded location.
Once there he reveals two bottles, each containing an identical-looking pill: one is harmless, the other is poison.
To play the game, he invites his victims to choose one, promising he will swallow the other — and he threatens to shoot them if they refuse.
The detective soon deduces that the driver is an estranged father who was told three years earlier he was dying.
The driver admits that he has a "sponsor" for his "work", receiving money for his children for each murder.
The detective, having noticed that the gun is a novelty cigarette lighter, attempts to leave.
However, the driver re-challenges him to choose a pill and see if he can beat the cabbie at the game.
Meanwhile, the doctor has traced the GPS signal from the phone and followed the two men.
He shoots the driver through a window in the adjacent building before the detective can swallow the pill he had chosen.
The detective demands that the cabbie reveal whether he chose the safe pill and the name of his sponsor.
The cabbie only yells out the sponsor's name before dying.
The police arrive, and the detective deduces that the shooter is the doctor, but hides the truth from the police.
The detective and the doctor leave the scene, encountering the detective's enigmatic "arch-enemy", who is revealed to be the detective's elder brother, who works for the British government.
The doctor discovers that the detective's brother tried to bribe him out of genuine concern for the detective.
The detective's brother instructs his assistant to increase their surveillance status.
On September 6, 1894, the detective stares out of his window, bored that he has no case to solve that is worthy of his talents.
He learns that a young Māori manservant, who works for a captain, has mysteriously disappeared.
The detective quickly deduces not only that the servant has been kidnapped, but also that two men – one significantly larger than the other – were responsible.
A few leads point to the docks by the river, and there, the detective and the physician learn that similar kidnappings of foreigners have occurred.
Further investigation leads them to an abandoned subterranean temple, where they discover a bloody and tortured corpse upon a sacrificial altar.
They also find opium with morphine which leads the detective to deduce that it is being used as a kind of soporific to subdue victims, so that they can be abducted and trafficked out of the country.
After finding a crate labelled "the institute", the detective recalls that the mountain flower Edelweiss (Leontopodium alpinum) is a national symbol of the alpine country.
Upon arrival it is discovered that the institute is a Swiss mental asylum headed by a gentleman, the asylum doctor.
The detective and the physician hatch a plan to gain access and investigate.
Knowing that he is about to willingly fall into the hands of criminals, the detective sends the physician away from the asylum.
This is primarily for his own safety, but also so that the detective still has a connection with the outside world should things go awry once inside the institute.
Donning a costume and assuming a false identity, the detective enters and is quickly incarcerated.
After escaping from his cell, he finds further proof of the asylum doctor's involvement in serious criminal activities.
Not only has the doctor been performing dangerous experiments on helpless victims in the asylum, he is also part of a cult awaiting the arrival of "the One".
The drugs provided were paid for with precious stones in the American city.
The detective unexpectedly discovers that his nemesis the master criminal is a patient, though a weakened shadow of his former self having survived the fall at the waterfall.
Using the master criminal as a distraction, the detective extricates himself from the asylum.
The detective and the physician travel to the American city to intercept the transfer of the stones.
They are soon taunted and harassed by the local sheriff who recognises them and appears to have some connection to the cult.
They learn that the stones were sold to the bank by the butler of a local man known as the householder.
Both the householder and his servant, a young lad, have been missing for days.
They find the lad, who is mute due to psychological trauma.
After the physician treats him, the lad writes on a chalkboard a series of numbers, which the physician copies down.
The detective and the physician then rescue the householder, who was about to be sacrificed by a crazed cult member deep in the swamp, and retrieve an ancient book.
Back in the capital, the detective and the physician learn from the book about a mythical sea god who could be awakened by the sacrificing of persons representing the different nations.
They also decipher the lad's numbers, which they find are co-ordinates pointing to a lighthouse on a Scottish coastline.
Once at the lighthouse, the detective and the physician have a final confrontation with the cultists and their leader the nobleman, whose fortune finances the sect.
The detective manages to stop the "summoning", but a fierce storm appears, which the nobleman assumes is the coming of the sea god.
Despite the detective's attempt to stop him, the nobleman jumps to his death into the raging sea below.

Upon returning to the capital, the physician plans to write their adventure into a book, however the detective tells him to not do it as the knowledge they have witnessed may fall into the wrong hands, which the physician thankfully accepts.

In September 1882, the detective takes up a case brought to him by his friend and roommate, the doctor: the Maori servant of one of the doctor's patients, the captain, has mysteriously disappeared from the man's estate.
After surveying the house's grounds, the detective concludes the servant was drugged, kidnapped and taken to the capital's port.
Upon further investigation at the port, the detective and the doctor find out several foreign workers have been disappearing after taking work from a smuggler known by a nickname.
The duo search a warehouse the smuggler operates out of and, during the search, the detective is struck by visions of impossible, otherworldly environments.

After the doctor helps the detective overcome these visions, the pair find a cult's ritual site underneath the warehouse, where an American private investigator who'd been looking into the smuggler was killed in a human sacrifice and the kidnapped victims were packed into crates and shipped off out of the country.
A review of the evidence leads the detective to conclude that the victims were transported to the institute, a psychiatric hospital in the mountain country.
In the mountain country, the doctor procures a meeting with the institute's director, the professor, by pretending to be interested in studying the asylum's treatment techniques.

Meanwhile, the detective poses as the murdered American investigator to try to force his way into an inspection of the premises, only for the professor to see through his ruse and have him forcefully sedated and confined in the asylum.

After regaining consciousness, the detective picks the lock on his cell and begins investigating the building; discovering that the professor has been performing unethical, mind altering procedures on the people kidnapped by the smuggler and shipped to her institution at the behest of a cult led by a British aristocrat.

With the aid of a man, a patient who believes himself to be an emperor, and another, a woman, whose doll orders her to kill people, the detective gets a message to the doctor about what he's uncovered.
Deciding to conduct his own research, the doctor discovers the former director of the institute, the predecessor, was forcibly lobotomized by the professor and committed to the institution.

He uses this knowledge to make a fake note from the predecessor which gets the professor out of her office and allows him to search it, where he finds evidence that the payments from the cult are being made with precious stones through an auction house in the southern city.

The doctor helps the detective escape from the patient wing of the asylum, after which the pair discover that the professor has been murdered by the woman, whom the detective unwittingly helped escape.

The duo travel to the southern city to investigate the auction house through which the professor and the smuggler's client paid them for their services, but their efforts are impeded by the lawman, the corrupt local police chief.

Nevertheless, with the assistance of a local madame and an informant, the detective and the doctor find out the man delivering the precious stones to the auction house was the butler of a local businessman.
The detective and the doctor travel to the businessman's mansion in the old quarter and find a young black woman outside the gates of the estate.
She claims her mute, younger brother, the boy, who works for the businessman, has been missing for days and she has been unable to get inside the property.
The duo find a way inside and discover a massacre has taken place at the mansion, where several workers were killed and the businessman was kidnapped and taken into the swamp.
During their investigation, the pair are hindered once more by the lawman, who tries to lynch the young woman as a threat, but the doctor manages to save her.
The detective pieces together that the butler kidnapped the businessman and killed the servants when they interrupted.
The boy also witnessed this but managed to avoid the butler by locking himself inside a room, where he has been hiding ever since.
The young woman talks the boy into unlocking the room and telling the investigators everything he knows about the butler and the businessman.
With this information and other clues found in the mansion, the detective deduces that the butler worked for the cult unbeknownst to the businessman.
He also finds out the businessman was in a secret relationship with the madame, so the pair next speak to her and inform her about her lover's kidnapping.
Shaken, the madame tells them the businessman suspected the butler was involved in some kind of criminal operation and had once followed him to a secret lair in the bayou.

The detective and the doctor travel into the bayou with a boat borrowed from the informant and, after avoiding an ambush by the lawman and his posse, they discover the ritual site, where they find the businessman, delirious and wounded but alive, as well as a strange book bound in human skin.
The detective suffers from more vivid visions of impossible underwater structures and has to be rescued by the doctor after he nearly has a mental breakdown.
The pair return the businessman to a grateful madame, who promises to help nurse him back to health and also begins plotting with the informant to take revenge on the lawman.

The investigators return to the capital and, while the detective rests to recover from nightmares he's suffered since the southern city, the doctor seeks the aid of a bookshop owner and occult researcher.

With his help and that of the detective's overbearing, government agent brother, the doctor determines the cult's leader is a nobleman, who is preparing a ritual of mass human sacrifice at a lighthouse in the northern country to awaken an ancient deity.
The detective and the doctor travel to the lighthouse in the middle of a violent storm.
They find that the butler had mutilated himself to death after being driven mad by visions, and are later confronted by the smuggler, whom the doctor manages to subdue and tie up.

Atop the structure, the nobleman is conducting a ritual involving obsidian crystals that keep the brainwashed kidnapped victims hypnotized, whom he directs to sacrifice themselves to the ancient beings by jumping from the lighthouse.
The detective distracts the nobleman while the doctor destroys the crystals to free the entranced victims.

The cult leader tries to persuade the detective of the truth of his visions, insisting none of them were hallucinations or madness but rather the detective's superior mind perceiving the true reality others cannot bear, but the detective resists his influence and distracts him long enough for the doctor to rescue his victims.
Distraught at his ritual being disrupted, the nobleman throws himself into the sea as a giant tidal wave approaches.
The detective stands before the approaching wave, insisting he must see if the nobleman's proclamations were true, but he is dragged inside the safety of the lighthouse by the doctor.
Weeks later, the detective and the doctor are back in the capital.
The pair rescued all the surviving victims but the detective is still haunted by nightmares.
The doctor tries to write about the case, but the detective insists that word of the nobleman's actions should not be made public, lest other madmen be inspired to follow in his footsteps.
